t: Burma won independence from Britain in 1948 as a federal union of the Bamar majority and many ethnic minorities.
The army has ruled for most of the period since 1962, first through Ne Win's isolationist socialism and then through juntas.
Brief reforms after 2011 ended with the coup of 2021, which turned decades of borderland insurgency into nationwide war.
dyk: The Burmese diplomat U Thant, a close friend of Prime Minister U Nu, served as Secretary-General of the United Nations from 1961 to 1971, the first Asian in that post.
ev: Aung San and minority leaders agree to form a union at the Panglong Conference
The Union of Burma becomes independent on 4 January
General Ne Win seizes power and launches the Burmese Way to Socialism
A nationwide uprising is crushed and a new military junta takes power
The NLD of Aung San Suu Kyi wins an election the junta refuses to honour
Cyclone Nargis kills about 138,000 people in the Irrawaddy delta
Army operations drive over 700,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh
The military seizes power on 1 February, sparking nationwide armed resistance

f.founder: Aung San (negotiated independence); U Nu, first prime minister
